newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cochlear sees 96/97 profit touch lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cochlear sees 96/97 profit touch lower.

text.p: Bionic ear maker Cochlear Ltd said on Tuesday it saw a small reduction in its earnings for the year to June 30, 1997.
"The loss of (research and development) tax concessions will impact on the forecast 1996/97 year," chief financial officer Neville Mitchell told Reuters.
Asked if this would result in a lower 1996/97 profit, Jefferies said: "a small reduction, yes."
Cochlear earlier reported a net profit for the year to June 30, 1996 of A$10.86 million, slightly above its prospectus forecast of A$10.4 million.
Cochlear's managing director Catherine Livingstone told Reuters the company would not cut its research and development (R&D) level but would look at the rate it grew this expenditure.
"At our current levels of R&D, we will lose a benefit of about A$1 million after tax," Livingstone said.
However as a direct result of this Cochlear would now be able to pay partly franked dividends commencing from its 1996/97 interim dividend payout, she said.
Cochlear currently spends over A$11 million or 15 percent of revenue on R&D. Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said the R&D tax concession would fall to 125 percent from 150 percent.

Livingstone said Cochlear was currently in pre-clinical trials for a new implant and was confident the implant would move to a programme of clinical trials with controlled release by the end of calendar 1996.
"It is a new implant and body processor, but the most exciting part of it is the behind-the-ear processor which will be a first in terms of our markets," Livingstone said.
She said its U.S. competitor, Advanced Bionics, had received regulatory approval from U.S. authorities to use its device for profoundly hearing impaired adults, not children, in the past few days.

"We have projected that their (Advanced Bionics) sales will increase but on the other hand the performance of our current product is excellent and sets the standard for the industry," Livingstone said.
At 2.55 p.m. (0455 GMT), Cochlear shares were one cent lower at A$3.37.
